jobs.title: HR M&A & Integration Project Manager
jobs.excerpt: TTM Technologies, Inc.  – Publicly Traded US Company, NASDAQ (TTMI) – Top-5 Global Printed Circuit Board Manufacturer About TTMTTM Technologies, Inc.
jobs.description:
TTM Technologies, Inc. – Publicly Traded US Company, NASDAQ (TTMI) – Top-5 Global Printed Circuit Board Manufacturer

About TTM

TTM Technologies, Inc. is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency (“RF”) components, RF microwave/microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (“PCB”s). TTM stands for time-to-market, representing how TTM's time-critical, one-stop design, engineering and manufacturing services enable customers to reduce the time required to develop new products and bring them to market.

Additional information can be found at www.ttm.com

Position Overview

The HR M&A & Integration Project Manager provides dedicated project management support to the Human Resources function across all phases of the mergers and acquisitions lifecycle. From assisting in the preliminary HR assessment of potential business opportunities through coordinating due diligence activities and supporting post-close people integration, this role ensures that HR is well-organized, well-represented, and well-prepared at every stage of the deal process. Sitting within the HR function and reporting to senior HR leadership, this individual serves as the operational backbone of HR's M&A involvement — helping the team stay structured, on track, and aligned with broader deal timelines and integration objectives. The ideal candidate is a highly organized project management professional with a strong grounding in HR practices, a natural ability to collaborate across functions, and the professionalism to manage sensitive information with care and discretion.

Key Responsibilities

HR Due Diligence Support

Supports the HR team in coordinating and executing people-related due diligence activities for potential acquisitions, ensuring HR is organized, responsive, and thorough throughout the pre-close review process.

  • Assist HR leadership in coordinating the people-related due diligence process, including tracking open requests, organizing documentation, and monitoring completion against deal timelines.
  • Help compile and maintain HR due diligence data packages, including workforce demographics, headcount and compensation summaries, benefits plan overviews, organizational charts, and HR policy inventories.
  • Support the review and documentation of target company HR practices, employment agreements, labor relations, leave programs, and compliance posture, flagging potential risks for HR leadership review.
  • Assist in organizing and managing HR-related materials within virtual data rooms, ensuring documentation is accurate, complete, and appropriately structured for deal team access.
  • Help prepare HR due diligence findings, gap analyses, and risk summaries for presentation to senior HR leaders and deal teams.
  • Support HR's participation in preliminary assessments of potential acquisition targets by helping gather publicly available workforce information and assisting with organizational profile summaries.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of HR due diligence checklists, templates, and standard data request packages to ensure consistency across transactions.

Day 1 & HR Transition Readiness

Supports HR's preparation for a smooth and compliant transition at deal close, ensuring employees of the acquired organization experience a professional and well-coordinated onboarding into the company.

  • Assist in developing and tracking HR Day 1 readiness plans, including employee communications, offer letter or transfer letter preparation, benefits enrollment coordination, and HRIS onboarding activities.
  • Help coordinate the transition of acquired employees into company HR systems, payroll, and benefits programs, working closely with HR Operations, Payroll, and Benefits teams.
  • Support the preparation of HR-related employee-facing communications for deal announcement and close, ensuring messaging is timely, accurate, and aligned with the overall communications plan.
  • Assist in tracking and resolving HR-related transition issues and employee inquiries during the pre- and post-close period, escalating complex matters to HR leadership as appropriate.
  • Help coordinate new employee orientation and onboarding activities for acquired employee populations in partnership with HR Business Partners, HR Operations and Talent Management.

HR Integration Planning & Execution

Provides ongoing project management support to HR integration workstreams following deal close, helping the HR team deliver against integration objectives in an organized and timely manner.

  • Support the development and maintenance of HR integration project plans, tracking workstream milestones, deliverables, owners, and timelines across key HR functional areas including HR Operations, Payroll, Benefits, Talent Acquisition, and HR Business Partners.
  • Assist in facilitating HR integration workstream meetings, including preparing agendas, capturing action items, and following up on open items with HR team members.
  • Help prepare HR integration status updates and progress reports for inclusion in broader Integration Management Office (IMO) governance reporting and executive communications.
  • Monitor HR integration activities against defined timelines and escalate risks, delays, or resource constraints to HR leadership promptly.
  • Assist in tracking HR-related integration milestones such as benefits harmonization, policy alignment, job architecture mapping, compensation review, and HRIS consolidation.
  • Support HR's participation in cross-functional integration workstreams and IMO meetings, helping to ensure HR deliverables and dependencies are clearly represented.

Workforce & Organizational Transition Support

Assists HR Business Partners and HR leadership in managing people-related activities that arise from organizational changes associated with M&A transactions.

  • Support the coordination of workforce restructuring activities associated with integrations, including tracking role mapping, position eliminations, and employee transition timelines.
  • Assist in preparing materials related to organizational design, spans and layers analysis, and headcount reconciliation between acquired and legacy organizations.
  • Help coordinate activities related to retention programs, stay bonuses, and key talent identification efforts for acquired employee populations.
  • Support HR compliance activities associated with M&A transactions, including WARN Act coordination, ERISA notifications, and applicable state and local employment law requirements, in partnership with Legal and HR leadership.
  • Assist in coordinating labor relations activities where applicable, including union notification requirements and collective bargaining agreement review support.

Change Management & Employee Experience Support

  • Assist in the coordination of HR change management activities designed to support acquired employees through the transition, including communication planning, manager toolkits, and FAQ development.
  • Support the administration of employee engagement and cultural integration surveys, helping to compile results and prepare summary reports for HR leadership review.
  • Help coordinate HR-related town halls, listening sessions, and employee Q&A forums in partnership with HR Business Partners and Communications teams.
  • Assist in tracking cultural integration activities and employee sentiment indicators, flagging concerns to HR leadership for follow-up.

Process, Tools & Continuous Improvement

  • Help develop, maintain, and continuously improve HR M&A playbooks, due diligence checklists, integration plan templates, and transition toolkits to build organizational capability and institutional knowledge.
  • Support the use of project management and reporting tools (e.g., Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Power BI) to maintain visibility into HR M&A pipeline activity and integration workstream progress.
  • Assist in capturing and documenting lessons learned following each transaction to inform and improve future M&A processes across the HR function.
  • Support the identification of opportunities to standardize, automate, or streamline HR M&A processes to improve speed and efficiency across transactions.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 8-10 years of project management experience, with exposure to HR.
  • 5+ years of experience specifically supporting M&A, integrations, transformations, or other complex enterprise initiatives.
  • Working knowledge of core HR functional areas including benefits, payroll, HRIS, talent acquisition, and HR compliance.
  • Strong organizational and project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience preparing clear, professional materials for HR and business audiences.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); familiarity with HRIS platforms (e.g., Workday).
  • High degree of professionalism, discretion, and the ability to manage confidential employee and deal-related information with integrity.

Preferred

  • PMP, CAPM, or equivalent project management certification.
  • Familiarity with HR compliance requirements related to M&A transactions, including WARN Act, COBRA, ERISA, and applicable state regulations.
  • Experience with project management tools such as Smartsheet or Microsoft Project.
  • Experience with data visualization and reporting tools.
  • Background in change management.
  • Experience in a manufacturing, technology, or global enterprise environment.

Competencies

Description

HR Functional Knowledge

jobs.excerpt: About Us RSB – Roundtable on Sustainable Biomaterials is a global, multi-stakeholder organisation dedicated to driving the truly sustainable development of the bioeconomy.
jobs.description:
About Us

RSB – Roundtable on Sustainable Biomaterials is a global, multi-stakeholder organisation dedicated to driving the truly sustainable development of the bioeconomy. Frequently recognised as an industry leader in supply chain sustainability, RSB applies its best-in-class sustainability framework across sectors including aviation, chemicals, materials, and shipping.

Our small, dedicated team operates remotely from countries around the world, working collaboratively with a diverse base of member organisations, industry partners, and policymakers. For more information, please visit .

Purpose of This Call

RSB now invites eligible organisations and individuals to indicate their interest. Throughout this document, “Consultant” refers to both organisations and individuals. RSB is building a pre-approved External Consultant Roster: a qualified pool of selected specialists and organisations that will be called upon for project-based work over the next 2 years.

Consultants accepted onto the roster will complete a brief onboarding process to become familiar with RSB’s systems, ways of delivering services, and sustainability framework. When a specific project or capacity gap emerges, RSB will contact roster members whose profile best matches the assignment, share a defined scope of work, and invite them to submit a proposal.

Inclusion on the roster is an expression of readiness and fit and not a guarantee of immediate work or remuneration.

Requirements

The Service

The Power-to-X (PtX) & Advanced Biofuels Consultant will provide technical research, policy analysis and value-chain expertise on renewable hydrogen, PtX fuels and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) topics, to support RSB's work on PtX fuels, advanced biofuels, SAF policy, certification readiness, and related grant-funded programmes. Estimated time investment and budget are to be confirmed based on the agreed scope, daily rate, and project needs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support technical research, stakeholder mapping, policy analysis and drafting across RSB's PtX fuels and advanced biofuels work.
  • Analyse renewable electricity, hydrogen and CO₂ sourcing, as well as biomass and waste feedstocks, relevant to PtX fuel and advanced biofuel pathways.
  • Assess regional development opportunities, certification requirements, GHG accounting considerations, cross-sector resource dynamics, and international market access.
  • Contribute to specific areas of roadmap development and policy briefing outputs, with initial work expected to focus mainly on India and potential targeted support for MENA-related activities.
  • Support other team priorities across RSB’s PtX fuels and advanced biofuels portfolio as needed.

Indicative Outputs

Specific deliverables, estimated time input, and project duration will be clarified in the Terms of Reference (TOR) issued to shortlisted roster members when a project need is identified. Indicative output types may include, but are not limited to:

  • Technical research reports, policy briefs and roadmap inputs on PtX fuels, advanced biofuels and SAF.
  • Stakeholder mapping and consultation summaries.
  • Resource and feedstock assessments covering renewable electricity, hydrogen, eligible carbon sources, biomass and waste feedstocks.
  • Life-cycle GHG modelling and carbon accounting analysis relevant to PtX fuels.
  • Market, regulatory and certification-readiness analysis, including market-access requirements under frameworks such as EU RED, ICAO CORSIA and UK SAF policy.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Essential

  • Strong written and spoken English proficiency.
  • Ability to maintain regular availability overlapping with CET working hours of a minimum of 4 hours per day.
  • Proven output/delivery track record in your area of expertise.
  • Full compliance with all applicable local laws and regulations, including tax and social security obligations, and legal authorisation to perform consultancy services in the country of residence or operation.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, the ability to operate autonomously, and a proactive approach to communicating progress, risks, and opportunities in a clear and constructive manner.
  • Self-sufficiency in a remote and fully digital working environment with reliable internet connectivity. Video calls and collaborative tools will be used for coordination.

For organisations:

  • Ability to assign appropriately qualified personnel to assignments and to ensure continuity of delivery, including cover for absences.
  • Confirmation that the named individuals proposed for RSB assignments meet the essential criteria above.

Desirable (will strengthen your expression of interest):

  • Demonstrated technical expertise in PtX fuels, renewable hydrogen technologies, advanced biofuels, or sustainable aviation fuel pathways.
  • Familiarity with EU RED or ICAO CORSIA regulatory frameworks, and with relevant regulatory and certification requirements more broadly, including UK SAF policy.
  • Demonstrated understanding of global PtX fuel and advanced biofuels developments, including key project trends, market-access requirements, and the role of renewable electricity, hydrogen, eligible carbon, and sustainable feedstocks.
  • Track record of producing original technical content, including resource assessments, policy analysis, roadmap inputs, applied sustainability analysis, or certification-related analysis, rather than literature summaries only.
  • Knowledge of renewable hydrogen, PtX and advanced biofuel production routes and value chains.
  • Understanding of key scale-up challenges, including renewable electricity, eligible carbon sources, sustainable feedstocks, hydrogen infrastructure, project bankability, certification readiness, and market recognition.
  • Familiarity with life-cycle GHG analysis and accounting approaches relevant to PtX fuels.
  • Awareness of PtX market and policy trends.

Benefits

For Consultants, this model offers a meaningful advantage: by completing the pre-qualification process once, you avoid repeated tender submissions and gain direct access to RSB’s pipeline of project-based opportunities as they emerge, with a relationship and context already in place.

Working with RSB offers the opportunity to contribute to a globally recognised organisation at the forefront of sustainability and systems transformation.

  • Meaningful, mission-driven work: Contribute to advancing sustainability standards and real-world impact across global value chains, influencing how industries operate and evolve.
  • High-impact assignments: Participate in intellectually engaging, project-based work that allows you to apply your expertise to real-world challenges.
  • Opportunity for ongoing collaboration: Consultants on the roster may be engaged on multiple assignments, fostering longer-term professional relationships with RSB.

Engagement Terms

Type of Engagement: Project-based (as required) with an overarching Framework Agreement

Remuneration: Agreed day rate

Location: Remote

Working Hours / Time Zone: Minimum 4 hours per day overlapping with CET/CEST.

Framework Agreement Duration: Initially until September 2028 [2 years], unless a Consultant or RSB request removal or changes to Framework Agreement.

Roster Project Launch: October 2026

OVERVIEW

The Company

U.S. Financial Technology (U.S. FinTech) is seeking an experienced Senior Director of Information Security to join our team of talented professionals. This is a full-time remote opportunity.

U.S. FinTech built and operates the largest and most advanced mortgage securitization platform in the world, supporting the Uniform Mortgage-Backed Security (UMBS) of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

Supporting 70% of the mortgage-backed securities in the market, U.S. FinTech provides best-in-class single-family issuance, bond administration, disclosure, and tax services. We support a broad portfolio of products for our clients with full lifecycle management.

Our market-leading, cloud-based, end-to-end platform executes transactions on an extraordinary scale which has bolstered liquidity in the secondary mortgage market, one of the largest and most important financial markets in the world. Our unique approach to securitization combines the best minds in financial services with the know-how, flexibility, and innovation of leading technologists.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Job Information

The Senior Director of Information Security will lead the overall design of cyber security architecture, cyber security engineering and business architecture to ensure that the organization is compliant to cyber security policies both internally and externally. This position will contribute to the overall security vision and strategy.  The focus will be on improving operational efficiencies and reliability within U.S. FinTech’s Cyber Security tools ecosystem while continuing the teams to work in an increasingly cloud native environment as we are completely cloud based.  This position will lead day-to-day management and execution of Cyber security architecture and engineering functions across all divisions.  This position will interface with IT professionals as well as leaders of the business to assess and manage cyber risk, share the security vision, and solicit involvement in achieving higher levels of enterprise security through information sharing and collaboration.  This is a successor type role for all across InfoSec's functional areas.

Key Job Functions

  • Partner with leaders across the business to identify opportunities and risks and develop solutions that support U.S. FinTech, a SaaS company serving as the critical backbone of the US mortgage finance industry.

  • Refine, design, and implement company-wide cyber security architecture and engineering in partnership with 2nd and 3rd lines of defense.

  • Develop cyber security patterns to enable developers to design and build applications with appropriate security controls.

  • Manage external assessment activities and synthesize information into senior level presentations.

  • Serves as a subject matter expert to internal business, technology, and security teams. Proactively advises on a range of cyber risk management activities and information security industry best practices.

  • Acts as an ambassador and senior technical advisor for enterprise cyber security while engaging with other senior technical leaders throughout the organization.

  • Develop and refine standards in partnership with Engineering, Infrastructure, Application Development, Data.

  • Maintain vigilance about current threat vectors and expertise of the ecosystem of cloud security-related tools.

  • Prototype new security tools and technologies based on organizational strategy and evolving threats while looking for opportunities to optimize, consolidate and manage out tools that no longer meet company needs.

  • Engage in ongoing communication with peers in the Infrastructure and Application Support groups as well as the business group to ensure understanding of security goals, to solicit feedback and foster cooperation.

  • Oversee deployment, integration, and initial configuration of all new cyber security solutions and enhancements to existing information security solutions in accordance with Information security policies, standards, and operational procedures.

  • Lead initiatives designed to share knowledge across cyber security, technology, and business teams. Identifies, recommends, coordinates, and delivers timely knowledge to support teams regarding technologies, processes, or tools.

  • Create and maintain a set of metrics to document and measure the performance and effectiveness of the Information Security program; responsible for communicating metrics to IT Leadership Team.
  • Lead the organization's identity and access management program, including identity lifecycle management, access governance, privileged access, and authentication controls.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in related discipline. Advanced degrees (MS, PhD) strongly preferred.
  • Industry Certification required, e.g. CISSP, CISA, CISM or equivalent designation.

Minimum Experience

.

Position Summary

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.

The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Risk Management

  • Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.
  • Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.
  • Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.
  • Provide independent oversight of business decisions and strategic initiatives.
  • Promote a strong risk culture throughout the organization.

Credit Risk Management

  • Oversee retail credit portfolios, including:
    • Mortgages
    • Personal Loans
    • Credit Cards
    • Auto Loans
    • Consumer Finance Products
  • Establish underwriting standards and credit policies.
  • Monitor portfolio quality, delinquency trends, and loss performance.
  • Lead stress testing and credit risk scenario analyses.
  • Recommend risk-adjusted lending strategies.

Operational Risk Management

  • Develop frameworks to identify and manage operational risks.
  • Monitor operational incidents, control failures, and emerging risks.
  • Oversee business continuity and operational resilience programs.
  • Strengthen internal controls and risk reporting mechanisms.
  • Ensure effective risk and control self-assessment processes.

Regulatory Compliance & Conduct Risk

  • Ensure compliance with banking regulations and consumer protection laws.
  • Oversee conduct risk management and fair customer treatment initiatives.
  • Maintain strong relationships with regulatory authorities.
  • Lead regulatory examinations and risk-related audits.
  • Ensure implementation of regulatory changes and risk controls.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk

  • Oversee fraud prevention, detection, and investigation programs.
  • Strengthen anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing controls.
  • Monitor financial crime risks and emerging threats.
  • Ensure effective transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting.
  • Collaborate with law enforcement and regulatory agencies when necessary.

Market & Liquidity Risk Oversight

  • Monitor interest rate risk and liquidity risk exposures.
  • Evaluate balance sheet vulnerabilities and stress scenarios.
  • Support asset-liability management activities.
  • Ensure adherence to regulatory capital and liquidity requirements.

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

  • Oversee technology and cyber risk governance.
  • Assess cybersecurity threats and resilience capabilities.
  • Ensure robust controls for digital banking platforms.
  • Monitor third-party and vendor risk exposures.
  • Support digital transformation initiatives through effective risk management.

Governance & Reporting

  • Present risk reports to Executive Management, Risk Committees, and the Board.
  • Develop key risk indicators (KRIs) and risk dashboards.
  • Ensure timely escalation of significant risk issues.
  • Maintain effective risk governance structures and committee frameworks.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Lead risk management teams across multiple disciplines.
  • Develop future risk leaders and succession plans.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and transparency.
  • Promote collaboration across business, compliance, audit, and technology functions.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Risk Management, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree (MBA, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field) preferred.

Professional Certifications

Preferred certifications include:

  • Financial Risk Manager (FRM)
  • Professional Risk Manager (PRM)
  • Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
  • Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive banking and risk management experience.
  • Extensive experience within retail banking risk management.
  • Proven leadership experience overseeing enterprise risk functions.
  • Experience interacting with regulators, boards, and executive committees.
  • Strong understanding of consumer lending, deposits, payments, and digital banking.
  • Experience leading large, multidisciplinary risk teams.

Technical Competencies

  • Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
  • Retail Credit Risk
  • Operational Risk
  • Regulatory Compliance
  • Financial Crime Risk
  • Fraud Risk Management
  • AML/KYC Frameworks
  • Market Risk
  • Liquidity Risk
  • Capital Adequacy Management
  • Cybersecurity Risk
  • Operational Resilience
  • Stress Testing
  • Risk Analytics & Modeling
  • Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)

Leadership Competencies

  • Strategic Leadership
  • Risk-Based Decision Making
  • Executive Communication
  • Board & Regulatory Engagement
  • Crisis Management
  • Ethical Leadership
  • Stakeholder Management

jobs.excerpt: W Base naszą misją jest wspieranie przedsiębiorców w podbijaniu globalnego e-commerce.
jobs.description:
W Base naszą misją jest wspieranie przedsiębiorców w podbijaniu globalnego e-commerce. Jesteśmy jedną z najszybciej rozwijających się platform w branży – w ciągu ostatnich 3 lat urośliśmy 15-krotnie! Dostarczamy system all-in-one dla tysięcy sprzedawców, integrując ich z Amazon, eBay czy Shopify.

Ale technologia to nie wszystko. W tym zespole cenimy inżynierską rzetelność i ludzką przyzwoitość. Nie szukamy "Ninja" ani "Rockstara". Szukamy Partnera, któremu możemy zaufać.

Zarządzanie infrastrukturą, która obsługuje miliony zapytań, to rola wysokiego zaufania. Dlatego szukamy osoby o mocnym kręgosłupie moralnym.

Twój Stack Technologiczny

Pracujemy na solidnym, wydajnym stacku. Musisz go znać od podszewki

  • Core: Linux (Debian/Ubuntu), Nginx (głęboki tuning i optymalizacja), PHP-FPM
  • Cloud: AWS (EC2, S3, RDS, VPC, Lambda, IAM)
  • Data: MySQL, Redis, RabbitMQ
  • Observability: Datadog, ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana)
  • IaC: Terraform / Ansible

Twoje zadania

  • Będziesz zarządzać uprawnieniami do infrastruktury. Oczekujemy pedantycznej dbałości o to, kto i dlaczego ma dostęp do serwerów
  • Wdrażanie koncepcji stabilnego działania usług w chmurze AWS, które wytrzymają nasz dynamiczny wzrost
  • Utrzymanie serwerów Unix/Linux – konfiguracja, aktualizacje i automatyzacja, z pełnym zrozumieniem tego, co dzieje się w systemie operacyjnym
  • Reagowanie na incydenty w oparciu o głęboką analizę logów (DD, Elastic). Szukanie przyczyn źródłowych (Root Cause Analysis), a nie tylko restartowanie usług
  • Wspieranie zespołów programistów, aby zapewnić ciągłą i płynną pracę systemu

Czego oczekujemy?

  • Min. 4 lata doświadczenia: W roli DevOps/SysAdmin, w tym praktyka z AWS
  • Bardzo dobra znajomość chmury, ale popartej doświadczeniem w klasycznej administracji (mile widziana przeszłość w utrzymaniu serwerów fizycznych/Data Center)
  • Swobody w Linuxie: Terminal to Twoje naturalne środowisko pracy
  • Moralności i Odpowiedzialności: Podejście "Can Do" łączysz z odpowiedzialnością za powierzone "klucze do królestwa".
  • Pokorny wobec technologii: Wiesz, że każdy popełnia błędy, ale Ty wiesz jak to naprawić
  • Analizuje problem "360 stopni": Patrzysz na problem z każdej strony – bezpieczeństwa, wydajności i długofalowych skutków
  • Łączy chmurę z "metalem": Pracujemy na AWS, ale szukamy kogoś, kto rozumie fizyczną naturę serwera
  • Języka: Angielski min. B2 (pracujemy globalnie)

Mile widziane

  • Certyfikaty AWS (potwierdzające wiedzę)
  • Praktyczna znajomość Terraform
  • Znajomość Apache Kafka lub Cloudflare
  • Chęć rozwoju w kierunku agentowego DevOps (automatyzacja procesów)

Co oferujemy?

  • Środowisko, w którym błędy traktujemy jak lekcje. Jeśli coś pójdzie nie tak – naprawiamy to razem, bez szukania winnych
  • Dołączysz do zespołu ludzi solidnych i pomocnych – to najlepszy program rozwojowy, jaki oferujemy
  • Twoja praca bezpośrednio przekłada się na stabilność biznesów tysięcy sprzedawców na świecie
  • Wynagrodzenie adekwatne do Twojej wiedzy i odpowiedzialności + pakiet benefitów wspierających zdrowie i rozwój

Job Description:

COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Hobart Service and Parts, both part of Illinois Tool Works (ITW), have been supporting the food equipment industry for over 125 years. With more than 1,800 associates nationwide, we serve as trusted partners to our customers—helping keep their operations running efficiently. Our employees are committed to delivering exceptional customer service, giving back to the communities where they live and work, and living out ITW’s core values of Integrity, Simplicity, Trust, Respect, and Shared Risk.

SUMMARY
Reporting to the Director of Business Development and Sales, the Regional Parts Sales Manager builds, maintains, and expands relationships with customers, channel partners, and internal stakeholders, to support growth in the aftermarket parts sales business. The main objective for the Regional Parts Sales Manager is to drive increased parts sales revenue while maintaining or growing margin in a competitive relationship-driven market. This role is responsible for achieving sales, profitability, and other sales orientated objectives, while supporting the entire range of aftermarket service parts sales and customer segments within their territory, to drive growth through collaboration, exploration, and alignment of opportunities.

This position will require a high-energy, results driven individual that is equipped to take on growth initiatives for the Hobart Parts division, develop strategic business plans, and oversee performance and productivity of designated customers and channel partners to achieve results. Applicants must have proven ability to perform in an environment that supports shared risk-taking, along with the ability to influence business partners and drive accountability through contractual requirements, processes, and relationship building.

The ideal candidate will be able to cultivate and grow business with existing clients, while identifying and developing new partnerships across multiple levels within their region.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Regional Parts Sales Manager will be responsible for supporting and executing revenue growth plans to increase the ITW FEG parts market penetration. This leader is responsible for profitable revenue growth through existing and new channels utilizing the ITW 80/20 and Front-To-Back (FTB) methodologies. This is a critical role for the parts business and is responsible to provide business results to achieve annual revenue growth. Key deliverables include:

  • Drive Revenue Growth: Responsible for creation and implementation of sales objectives and strategies. Track performance metrics for sales channels to create focus and drive continuous improvement. Support service parts financial planning and monthly revenue outlook. Achieve outlook for sales and margin goals. Partners with channel partners to develop relevant, timely and successful sales plans, campaigns, programs, and special promotions to drive parts revenue growth.

Develop, recommend, and implement process and system enhancements designed to streamline performance and capability with focus on continuous improvement.

Effectively research market and industry trends providing critical intelligence for strategic planning. Leverage voice-of-the-customer (VOC) feedback processes to prioritize tactical and strategic initiatives driving customer-focused solutions.

  • Exceptional communication and presentation skills, both verbal and written
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Excellent decision-making skills
  • Strong negotiating skills
  • Project management skills

jobs.title: Dedicated Care Coordinator Mid West
jobs.excerpt: Why Patients Need YouThe Inflammation and Immunology Dedicated Care Coordinator (DCC) is a non-promotional, field-based role that supports patients’ access to PDPA and VFM products when prescribed by a licensed healthcare provider.
jobs.description:
Why Patients Need You

The Inflammation and Immunology Dedicated Care Coordinator (DCC) is a non-promotional, field-based role that supports patients’ access to PDPA and VFM products when prescribed by a licensed healthcare provider. The DCC owns the continual management and progression of the patient journey — from HUB enrollment through post-fill follow-up — working directly with patients, providers, payers, HUB partners, and third-party vendors. It is a dual patient- and HCP-facing role spanning a patient journey, and the colleague in this role carries 100% ownership of every case in their assigned geography.

What You Will Achieve

The DCC is a subject-matter expert on reimbursement, access, and coverage issues that can educate patients/caregivers and healthcare providers on matters relating to reimbursement, access, and coverage. The DCC will serve as the primary point of contact for patients/caregivers and healthcare providers regarding the status of their request for reimbursement support and access assistance and will also provide updates to patients/caregivers and healthcare providers on their status as appropriate. The DCC holds end-to-end case ownership: benefits investigation and verification, prior authorization and appeals support, appointment and baseline assessment coordination, Interim Care and voucher administration, copay support, prescription triage, and scheduled post-fill follow-up.

How You Will Achieve It

Case Ownership and the Patient Journey

  • Own 100% of assigned cases and drive the continual management and progression of the patient journey, from HUB enrollment through post-fill follow-up

  • Be the central point-of-contact for patients/caregivers and HCP providers regarding the status of their request for reimbursement and access support related to a patient case.

  • Answer questions from patients/caregivers relating to access and coverage

  • Maintain a clear understanding of the patient access journey and requirements at each stage of the process, as well as the role played by patients/caregivers and HCP providers in the process

  • Support access with HCPs and opted-in patients/caregivers who have been prescribed a PDPA OR VFM product

Benefits Investigation and Financial Navigation

  • Conduct the Summary of Benefits (SOB) discussion required for every HUB-enrolled patient, reviewing both the product benefit structure, any associated cost and the baseline appointments for VFM

  • Obtain all missing information on the Patient Enrollment Form (PEF) and verify the testing, voucher, and Interim Care options selected by the HCP office

  • Walk the patient through out-of-pocket cost, deductibles, copay options, and the reimbursement program, including the impact of maximizers and accumulators

  • Verify coverage for the product and for required baseline tests across both PBM and major medical insurance for VFM

  • Oversee the entire prior authorization process, including submission and verification with both the patient and the provider

  • Conduct benefit investigation and verification (BI/BV) calls directly with payers and patients for patients with 3rd party restrictions

  • Confirm and communicate product coverage, cost, prior authorization and appeal requirements, Interim Care program PA and Appeal deadlines, and baseline assessment tests to HCP and patient

Appointment and Assessment Coordination

  • Schedule, reschedule and confirm patient appointments in coordination with the patient, the provider, and the vendor

  • Secure the appropriate confirmation communication back from the provider (CFT)

  • Coordinate compliantly with IQVIA/MDX on patient assessment tests — confirm tests are completed and reschedule where needed

Program and Copay Administration

  • Once IC is approved, manage all Interim Care (IC) program administrative requirements and deadlines with the provider and the patient, including Extended Interim Care programs

  • Confirm voucher need and eligibility with the provider and patient, and triage the voucher for shipment to the patient

  • Maintain Copay portal access and help approved commercial patients secure a copay card

  • Own copay eligibility attestation responsibility

  • Follow up with the patient post-fill to confirm the copay card is functioning correctly

Prescription Triage, Fulfillment, and Ongoing Follow-Up

  • Triage the voucher, paid prescription, and/or Interim Care fill within Polaris

  • Contact the patient at 10 days and again at 45 days post-prescription, confirming that no logistical or financial questions remain outstanding

Case and Systems Ownership

  • Manage and update various case types in Polaris, using its texting, faxing, and prescription triage capabilities

  • View and interpret prior authorization, appeal, and PEF documentation for accuracy

  • Share and manage cases with HUB partners across all patient journeys

  • Coordinate as appropriate with other Pfizer colleagues and Patient Support Program/HUB employees, via tasks and secure messages to requests for action, to help resolve problems with individual patient cases

  • Maintain case comments as a real-time account of the patient journey, including a recap of every call made to the HCP and the patient

  • Use the Kite works encrypted email system for correspondence with patients and providers

  • Manage the Docusign process with patients to obtain required consents

  • Develop an organized, concise, and compliant way to manage assigned patient cases within established time frames

Compliance, Safety Reporting, and Communication

  • Report adverse events (AEs) in accordance with company requirements — AE reporting volume is elevated in this role, patient contact is more frequent and spans the entire patient journey

  • Operate within the tighter content controls and system permissions that apply to this role

  • Compliantly communicate the access landscape and options to patients/caregivers and HCPs

  • Link the patient access support to meet patient needs, using Brand RC-approved materials

  • Conduct yourself with the utmost discretion and confidentiality

  • Adhere to strict company compliance guidelines and procedures

  • Work and lead cross-functionally with internal and external colleagues, compliantly, to improve the patient access journey

  • Effectively link customer insights to the offerings and approved resources to address patient access barriers

  • Build trust through compliant follow-up and knowledge of the access journey

  • Demonstrate excellence in responsible business communication, both written and spoken

Qualifications

Must-Have

  • B.S. or B.A. Degree 8+ years of pharmaceutical (or related) experience in customer-facing roles/functions.

  • 6 months minimum as a FRM, PAC, FAS or similar experience in access and Reimbursement and working with Polaris CRM System.

  • Working proficiency in Polaris, including case management and documentation, prescription triage, and interpretation of PA, appeal, and PEF documentation

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate directly with patients, with providers, and with cross-functional colleagues

  • Experience conducting benefit investigation and verification directly with payers, and working knowledge of prior authorization and appeals processes

  • Working knowledge of copay programs, copay maximizers and accumulators, vouchers, and free or interim care programs

  • Ability to own a high volume of concurrent cases across a patient journey that could average approximately 20 days, with disciplined documentation and follow-through

  • Ability to meet adverse event reporting obligations in a role with frequent, direct patient contact

  • Strong understanding of Reimbursement, Government Payment Systems, Specialty Pharmacy Networks, Co-Pay Assistance Programs, and knowledge of the Specialty Medication area.

  • Appropriate and compliant communication and collaboration with cross-functional field-based colleagues (Sales, Medical, FRM, PCA/SAS, KAD, Government Relations) to ensure optimal and appropriate patient access in both in-patient and out-patient accounts.

  • Alignment with HQ stakeholders to ensure appropriate understanding of, and support for patient access (e.g., Brand and Customer Marketing teams and PCA/SAS teams).

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience in a Patient and/or customer facing role requiring access and reimbursement education.

  • Experience working with a HUB.

  • Experience with Kite works or a comparable encrypted email platform, Docusign, and copay portal administration

  • Experience coordinating with third-party vendors on patient assessment, testing, or specialty pharmacy logistics (e.g., IQVIA/MDX, Sonexus)

  • Experience supporting Interim Care, free goods, or bridge programs

  • Experience with both pharmacy benefit (PBM) and major medical benefit coverage pathways

Knowledge & Skill Sets Desired:

  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Exceptional relationship building skills, especially with elderly age groups

  • Trust

  • Integrity

  • Empathy

  • Patience

  • Deliver meaningful & concise presentations

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills

  • Exceptional critical thinking skills, ability to understand complex processes and effectively communicate to diverse community of patients

  • Outstanding collaboration and networking abilities

  • Ability to work in a team environment

  • Understanding of Specialty Pharmaceuticals and Patient Journeys

  • Adherence to Regulatory and Compliance Standards

  • Flexibility to work across different time zones if needed

Other Job Details

  • Work Location Assignment: Remote colleagues from home 5 days a week or are field-based colleagues that are not affiliated with a Pfizer site.

  • Ability to travel – Approximately 10% to 20%

  • Time Zone: Central time zone.

  • Eligible for Relocation Package – NO

  • LAST DAY TO APPLY - 9/18/2026

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $162,900.00 to $271,500.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States.This role is posted in multiple locations. Where do you belong?

Your career is more than just a job, it's part of your life. We want you to love coming to work each day because you believe in what you do and the people with whom you work. We care about your success.

Job Description

The Coding Education Specialist researches complex coding issues and recommends resolutions. Identify training needs and develop processes. Skilled Coding Education Specialists are passionate educators who design, develop, and deliver engaging coding curricula to learners of various skill levels. This includes the ability to translate complex coding concepts into accessible learning experiences.

AHIMA or AAPC annual membership will be covered by USACS

  • Curriculum Development: Design and update coding lessons, projects, and assessments tailored to different learning objectives and audiences, including USACS and vendor coders.

  • Learner Support: Monitor student progress, provide feedback, and offer one-on-one or group support to ensure learner success.
  • Assessment & Reporting: Measure student performance through formative and summative assessments; analyze and report data to inform instructional improvements.
  • Community Engagement: Participate in external training programs by presenting tailored materials to engage interest in joining our internal coding team. Example: Stark State College coding program.
  • Resource creation & maintenance: Create and maintain coding resources that assist coders in applying organizational policy to broad coding concepts (e.g., SOPs, site pages, etc.).
  • Industry Monitoring: As a member of the Industry Monitoring team, research coding topics or issues, create problem statements, provide recommendations, develop and present education and/or continuous improvement updates.
  • Regular Collaborations with all RCM internal teams to ensure coding processes, guidelines, and policies are accurately applied.
  • Provide educational consultations for internal Coding Department staff when applicable. Assist in preparation for QA Webinars, quarterly coding meetings, and vendor calibration calls and actively participate in both.
  • Analyze and trend audit results to identify root causes, then create and launch targeted education. Followed by monitoring audit results to confirm expected improvement.
  • Create and launch coder edits to mitigate areas of risk, followed by monitoring to confirm expected results
  • Performs and assists with other department duties as needed.

  • Knowledge of and experience using ICD-10-CM and CPT coding.
  • Knowledge of payor and coding guidelines.
  • Knowledge of and skill in using personal computers in a Windows environment with an emphasis on Excel, Word, Adobe, PowerPoint, and Zoom.
  • Ability to pay close attention to detail, be multi-task oriented and work independently
  • Ability to identify research and solve problems and discrepancies.
  • Ability to communicate with employees, management, physicians, and vendors in a courteous professional manner.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Strong organizational skills with an ability to maintain multiple competing priorities

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • Emergency Department pro-fee coding experience

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for prolonged periods and occasionally walk, stand, bend, stoop, and lift up to 15 pounds.

Job Description: Chief Controls Officer (CCO – Controls)

Industry: Banking, Financial Services, Insurance, Investment

Job Type: Full-Time

Reporting To: Chief Risk Officer (CRO) / Chief Financial Officer (CFO) / Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

Job Summary

The Chief Controls Officer (CCO – Controls) is responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing the organization's internal control framework to ensure effective risk mitigation, regulatory compliance, and operational integrity. This role ensures that controls across financial, operational, and compliance processes are robust, consistent, and aligned with organizational risk appetite.

The CCO (Controls) plays a critical role in strengthening governance, preventing control failures, and enhancing transparency across all business functions.

Key Responsibilities

1. Internal Controls Framework

Develop and maintain enterprise-wide internal control frameworks (e.g., COSO)

Ensure controls are effectively designed, documented, and implemented

Standardize control practices across business units

Continuously improve control effectiveness and maturity

2. Control Monitoring & Testing

Oversee control testing, monitoring, and validation processes

Implement continuous control monitoring systems

Identify control gaps and weaknesses

Ensure timely remediation of control deficiencies

3. Risk & Compliance Integration

Align internal controls with enterprise risk management (ERM) frameworks

Collaborate with risk, compliance, and audit teams

Ensure controls support regulatory compliance requirements

Monitor emerging risks and adapt control frameworks accordingly

4. Financial & Operational Controls

Oversee financial controls, including reporting, reconciliation, and revenue controls

Ensure operational controls across processes, systems, and workflows

Strengthen fraud prevention and detection mechanisms

Ensure consistency in control execution

5. Governance & Policy Management

Develop and maintain control-related policies and procedures

Ensure documentation, audit trails, and governance standards are maintained

Support governance committees and reporting requirements

Enhance transparency and accountability

6. Technology & Controls Automation

Leverage technology and automation to enhance control effectiveness

Implement control tools, dashboards, and monitoring systems

Collaborate with IT on system controls and cybersecurity frameworks

Drive digital transformation in control environments

7. Stakeholder Engagement

Provide control insights and reporting to executive leadership and Board

Collaborate with regulators, auditors, and external stakeholders

Support internal and external audits

Promote awareness of control responsibilities across the organization

8. Leadership & Team Management

Lead and develop internal controls and governance teams

Establish performance standards and accountability

Foster a culture of control awareness and discipline

Support talent development and succession planning

Key Requirements

Education

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field

Professional certifications such as CPA, CIA, CISA, or equivalent are highly preferred

Experience

12–18+ years of experience in internal controls, audit, risk, or compliance roles

Proven experience in senior leadership roles (e.g., Chief Controls Officer, Head of Internal Controls)

Strong background in banking, financial services, insurance, or investment sectors

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of internal control frameworks (e.g., COSO)

Strong understanding of risk management and regulatory compliance

Expertise in financial and operational controls

Analytical and problem-solving skills

Leadership and team management

Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement

High attention to detail and governance mindset

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Effectiveness of internal control framework

Number and severity of control deficiencies

Timeliness of remediation actions

Compliance with regulatory and audit requirements

Reduction in control failures and operational risks

Audit and regulatory inspection outcomes

Preferred Attributes

Experience in multinational or highly regulated financial institutions

Exposure to IT controls, cybersecurity, and automation tools

Strong collaboration with risk, compliance, and audit functions

Ability to lead enterprise-wide control transformation initiatives

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive executive salary

Performance-based incentives

Executive benefits and allowances

EnableComp earned its reputation in the toughest corners of the revenue cycle by solving the complex claims no one else could. By cutting through complexity, we help hospitals thrive, resulting in recognition as Black Book’s #1 Specialty RCM provider for complex claims and revenue integrity in 2024 and 2025, a multi-year Top Workplaces honoree, and a SOC 2 Type II and HITRUST e1-certified platform.Our Vision is to empower healthcare providers to focus on patient care, not revenue cycle complexity. Our Mission is to uncover what others miss—turning every client dollar recovered into insight that helps prevent future loss. We live our Core Values of Uncompromising Integrity, Ecstatic Clients, and Empowered Team Members by operating with trust, accountability, and a “we before me” mindset. We pursue Innovation and Profitable Growth through continuous improvement and thoughtful problem-solving, and we believe work should include Fun—celebrating success, recognizing our people, and maintaining healthy work-life balance.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Manager, Demand Generation owns EnableComp’s demand generation engine — planning and executing the multi-channel campaigns that build pipeline, and, as our first dedicated content hire, creating the blog posts, ebooks, landing pages, and nurture content those campaigns run on. This role builds on the technical infrastructure the GTM Engineer maintains and the positioning the Director, Product Marketing sets, translating both into campaigns that generate and nurture qualified leads.

Reporting to the VP, Marketing, the Manager will partner closely with Product Marketing, the Commercial Enablement Director, the Manager of Event Marketing & Strategic Partnerships, and the SDR function to ensure a consistent, well-coordinated path from first touch to qualified pipeline. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports at this time.

The Job Responsibilities Include

  • Plan, build, and execute multi-channel demand generation campaigns across email, paid social, SEM, retargeting, and organic channels.
  • Own marketing-sourced pipeline targets and report on campaign performance against revenue goals.
  • Manage the demand generation budget, tracking spend against ROI and reallocating based on channel performance.
  • Own funnel content end-to-end: blog posts, ebooks/guides, landing pages, and nurture email copy that fuel campaigns — this is our first dedicated content hire, so the expectation is building the engine, not just staffing it.
  • Ensure all campaign content reflects current positioning and messaging maintained by the Director, Product Marketing.
  • Establish a scalable, repeatable content calendar and production workflow.
  • Build and manage lead nurture email programs and campaign workflows inside HubSpot, working within the lead scoring and account routing logic the GTM Engineer designs and maintains.
  • Partner with the GTM Engineer on campaign-specific automation needs and data requirements, without owning the underlying tech stack, integrations, or scoring/routing architecture.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot campaign-level workflow issues, escalating systemic or infrastructure issues to the GTM Engineer.
  • Partner with the Manager, Event Marketing & Strategic Partnerships on webinar and event promotion strategy, registration goals, and post-event lead nurture (Events owns strategy, logistics, and execution; Growth Marketing owns the pipeline goals and follow-up).
  • Partner with the Director, Product Marketing to ensure campaigns and content reflect current narrative, positioning, and competitive messaging.
  • Partner with the SDR function on lead handoff, MQL quality feedback, and conversion tracking.
  • Analyze campaign and content performance data to identify what’s working, kill what isn’t, and continuously optimize for MQL volume, conversion rate, and cost per acquisition.
  • Stay current on emerging channels and AI-powered marketing/content tools, piloting new tactics to keep programs ahead of the curve.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Requirements & Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field required; equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
  • 3–5 years of experience in demand generation, growth marketing, or a related B2B marketing role.
  • Experience in healthcare, healthcare technology, Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), or another complex B2B industry is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with marketing automation platforms (HubSpot preferred) and CRM systems (Salesforce).
  • Strong writing skills — comfortable independently drafting blog posts, email copy, and landing page copy, since this role owns content without a dedicated content team behind it.
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience pulling and interpreting campaign data to make decisions.
  • Comfort partnering with a technical GTM/RevOps function (e.g., a GTM Engineer) on automation and data needs without owning the underlying systems.
  • Regular and predictable attendance.
  • Must have strong computer proficiency and understand how to use office applications, including MS Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook), Zoom, and other learning technology.
  • To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Special Considerations & Prerequisites

  • Practices and adheres to EnableComp’s Core Values, Vision and Mission.
  • Individual contributor role; no direct reports at this time.
  • A great candidate is self-directed and comfortable owning ambiguous, cross-functional problems; treats data hygiene as non-negotiable; and can translate technical workflows into plain-language impact for Sales and Marketing stakeholders.
  • Strong project management and prioritization skills; comfortable running multiple campaigns simultaneously.
  • A bias toward experimentation and iteration, including piloting AI-enabled content and marketing tools.
  • Minimal travel required (less than 20%), primarily for occasional team or company offsites.
  • Ability to work at a computer for extended periods; standard office or remote work environment.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

About AccrediCulture

AccrediCulture is a healthcare compliance platform used by be​havioral health organizations for accreditation readiness, policy governance, chart compliance, incident and grievance management, credential tracking, clinical supervision documentation, and staff training.

Our training library includes more than 1,000 narrated video courses covering clinical practice, patient rights, safety, and regulatory topics. AccrediCulture is seeking continuing education provider approval from ASWB ACE, NBCC, and NAADAC so that eligible clinical courses can count toward the continuing education requirements of social workers, counselors, and addiction professionals.

The Opportunity

AccrediCulture is seeking a Continuing Education Advisor to serve as its designated Social Work Consultant under the ASWB ACE standards and as a clinical reviewer for its broader continuing education program.

This is a light, ongoing advisory opportunity for a licensed clinical social worker who is currently practicing or has previously practiced social work and would like to provide clinical judgment and oversight to a growing continuing education program.

Most assignments occur during the initial provider application process, when new courses are prepared for release, and during quarterly reviews of participant evaluations. The anticipated workload is approximately two to four hours per month.

What You Will Do

  • Serve as the named Social Work Consultant on AccrediCulture’s ASWB ACE provider application and throughout the approval period.
  • Review and sign the attestations required of the designated Social Work Consultant.
  • Review course learning objectives, descriptions, outlines, and bibliographies.
  • Confirm that courses fall within the social work scope of practice and an applicable ASWB educational area.
  • Participate in pilot testing for new self-paced courses.
  • Review pilot-testing results with the Continuing Education Director and recommend changes to course content, post-test questions, or proposed credit amounts.
  • Review course post-tests for clarity, fairness, and alignment with the stated learning objectives.
  • Confirm that course content reflects cultural awareness and diversity and recommend revisions when appropriate.
  • Review summarized participant evaluations each quarter.
  • Advise on course revisions, course retirements, and emerging topics relevant to social workers.
  • Participate in the review of participant grievances involving course content or instructors.
  • Advise on continuing education requirements in states where AccrediCulture’s client facilities operate.
  • Identify regulatory changes that may affect the continuing education program.
  • Assist the Continuing Education Director in responding to questions from ASWB, NBCC, or NAADAC reviewers that relate to the advisor’s responsibilities.
  • Maintain an eligible license in good standing and notify AccrediCulture within ten calendar days of any change in license status or contact information.

Requirements

  • Active, unrestricted LCSW license in good standing in at least one U.S. state.
  • No professional license disciplinary history.
  • Master of Social Work from a CSWE-accredited program.
  • At least five years of post-licensure clinical practice.
  • Current or previous experience practicing social work.
  • Ability to carefully review clinical and educational materials.
  • Ability to provide clear, practical written feedback within an agreed-upon timeframe, generally five business days.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Comfortable communicating through email and video meetings.
  • Comfortable accessing a learning management system and reviewing courses from a participant’s perspective.
  • Willingness to be named as AccrediCulture’s Social Work Consultant and sign applicable attestations.
  • Ability to maintain an active, unrestricted license throughout the engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in substance use disorder or co-occurring disorder treatment.
  • Familiarity with ASWB ACE, NBCC, or NAADAC continuing education standards.
  • Experience with curriculum or course review.
  • Experience developing or reviewing clinical training.
  • Clinical supervision experience.
  • Accreditation or regulatory compliance experience.
  • Experience reviewing examinations, participant evaluations, or educational grievances.

Benefits

This is an independent contractor opportunity and is not eligible for employee benefits.

  • Compensation of $100 to $125 per hour, depending on experience.
  • No minimum hours or fixed weekly schedule.
  • Work may be completed remotely.
  • Advisor sets their own working hours, subject to agreed-upon deadlines.
  • Monthly invoicing in quarter-hour increments.
  • Ongoing opportunity to contribute to the clinical quality of a growing continuing education program.

The independent contractor is responsible for their own taxes, insurance, equipment, and other business expenses.

Overview

We are looking for an AI-native, execution-minded Customer Journey Manager to own lifecycle performance across key post-enrollment customer journeys, with a specific focus on Retention, Winback, and Partner Cross-Sell. This role will focus primarily on the client servicing side of the customer lifecycle—helping customers stay engaged, remain successful in their program, return when appropriate, and discover relevant partner solutions that can provide additional value.

This is not a narrow campaign management role. It is a high-agency operator role for someone who can both run the work and improve how the work gets done. You will build and optimize campaigns, journeys, and tests across channels, while also strengthening the underlying processes, tools, workflows, and cross-functional orchestration that make lifecycle marketing faster, smarter, and more effective over time. Our team operates like a high-performing in-house agency within the broader organization. That means this role offers real ownership, high autonomy, broad visibility, direct access to leadership, and the opportunity to help shape how modern lifecycle marketing gets done here.

The right candidate combines lifecycle marketing craft, direct response instincts, experimentation rigor, platform adaptability, and unusually high personal agency. They do not wait around for a task list. They identify opportunities, figure things out, build better ways of working, and use AI and modern tooling in practical ways to improve performance, customer experience, speed, and operational efficiency.

  • Client Lifecycle Strategy, Retention & Journey Performance

This position is responsible for end-to-end report development, including gathering business requirements, sourcing and validating data from enterprise platforms such as Snowflake, developing SQL-based queries and data logic, and creating Power BI reports, dashboards, semantic models, and data visualizations that support operational decision-making, process improvement, and leadership insight.

This position has the ability to work remotely in any of the 40+ States in which TDS operates.

Responsibilities

Report Development, Testing, and Implementation

  • Utilize BI tools, including Power BI, to design, construct, test, deploy, and maintain reports, dashboards, scorecards, and data visualizations for Shared Services.
  • Translate business requirements into report specifications, data models, and visual reporting solutions that clearly communicate trends, exceptions, performance drivers, and actionable insights.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI reports, dashboards, semantic models, DAX measures, refresh schedules, and workspace content to support accurate and actionable reporting.
  • Develop, troubleshoot, and optimize SQL-based report logic, joins, transformations, and data extracts to support recurring and ad hoc reporting needs.

Report To: Delivery Manager

Job Location: Remote and/or London (right to work in UK or EU required)

Employment Status: Full Time

Who is ControlPlane?

ControlPlane is a London headquartered consultancy specialising in cloud-native, Kubernetes, and open source solutions. Our expertise lies in helping organisations adopt and secure complex cloud infrastructures by implementing security measures that are "secure-by-design" and "secure-by-default." This engineering excellence has driven ControlPlane deeper into cybersecurity providing services like threat modelling, penetration testing, and supply chain security to ensure robust protection against cyberattacks in containerised and cloud-native environments.

We are acclaimed for our contributions to securing highly regulated industries, such as finance, healthcare, and national infrastructure. We help businesses improve their security posture through services like DevSecOps consulting, zero-trust architectures, and platform engineering. ControlPlane also focuses on advancing best practices in the Kubernetes ecosystem, offering specialised training and community engagement.

Our clients range from multinational banks to tech giants and public clouds, where we assist with both security and operational needs. In addition to consulting, we are active in the open source community, supporting projects like Flux CD and providing security tools for Kubernetes environments.

Over the coming years you’ll see us retain our focus on solving difficult problems for clients with intense security controls using pragmatic, real world solutions. Taking our extensive R&D to help organisations consume next generation and open source projects safely and securely - that might be extending our work with FINOS AI Readiness or the overhaul of open source supply chain security.

What We're Looking For in a Cloud Native Security Consultant

We are looking for Cloud Native Security consultants to represent the technical and cultural values of ControlPlane, leading our customers by example in the complex and fast-changing world of cloud native technology. You will perform a mix of client consulting, working on internal labs projects, and contributing to Open Source projects on ControlPlane’s behalf.

There is no perfect candidate for this role. As we look to extend our cloud native security team we welcome engineers and architects with a diverse range of capabilities, experiences and backgrounds.

We are SANS authors (SEC584) and believe strongly in team learning and collaboration. Candidates with an aptitude to learn are preferred, and we provide full training for the newest cloud technologies that our customers rely on.

This is a unique job role within a successful start-up company where you will have the chance to make a positive impact, learn, grow and work with great colleagues who consistently challenge the status quo.

Roles, Responsibilities and Requirements of Our Cloud Native Security Consultant:

  • Knowledge of Threat Modelling and Cloud Native Security architectures (AWS, GCP, Azure)
  • Kubernetes and container experience (some of EKS, GKE, AKS, OpenShift, and container runtimes)
  • Knowledge of software supply chain security
  • DevSecOps principles and Engineering practices
  • CI/CD experience, automating security tests, and hardening pipelines
  • Knowledge of security tooling from enterprise tools such as Aqua, Prisma, Sysdig, Lacework, etc to Open Source tools such as falco, kube-hunter, and kube-bench.
  • Knowledge and experience using hardening guides, compliance and risk management standards

A desire to learn, or experience with:

  • CLI tooling in any of the above technologies.
  • Golang or Python
  • Terraform and cloud infrastructure best practices (IaC, regulated systems)

Benefits

ControlPlane is a dynamic, cutting edge and passionate business for which to work. Our employees are the heart of our business, which means we care about our company culture and our employees’ wellbeing and progression. Alongside this, as our colleague you will have the following benefits:

  • Generous and competitive salary
  • Bonus
  • 33 days of paid holiday, including paid leave for the standard 8 UK Bank Holidays
  • Enhanced Parental Leave
  • Private Medical insurance
  • An individual training budget for personal development, including but not limited to:
    • Conferences
    • Training (books, courses, coaching, as well as internal training which is of course included beyond budget)
    • Qualifications

We believe our peers are equally as important as the technology we use. We’re looking for people of the highest personal calibre, quietly confident, with a good work ethic, keenness to learn, emotional maturity and respect, who know that “we” is more than “me”, and who embrace human diversity of all kinds. As we grow you will help us to build a company culture of which we can all be proud. If you espouse these values, we want you!

NOTE FOR RECRUITMENT AGENCIES: Please do not call or email our team speculatively, we do not accept unsolicited CVs.

jobs.description:
Job Summary


The Senior Performance Engineer is responsible for expected-versus-actual energy performance across SunStrong’s serviced fleet, spanning residential systems, commercial and industrial sites, community solar, and utility-scale projects. This role models production, quantifies and defends contractual performance obligations, and drives underperformance to root cause with operations and field services. As the senior technical authority on fleet performance, the position sets the data requirements behind performance reporting, advises on dashboard and analytics development rather than building it, and partners with asset management and O&M on billing and settlement accuracy. The role sits on the Fleet Management Technology team and requires equal comfort with a residential inverter fleet, a metered utility-scale PPA settlement, and the data platform that carries both.

Responsibilities

  • Model and monitor energy performance across residential, C&I, community solar, and utility-scale assets in PlantPredict and the fleet monitoring platforms (AlsoEnergy, Power Factors, 3E), comparing metered production against simulation using weather and irradiance data from Solcast, SolarAnywhere, and Open-Meteo.
  • Calculate and defend contractual performance metrics including availability, performance ratio, production guarantees, and liquidated damages exposure, and produce the recurring analysis that supports billing, PPA and lease invoicing, and investor and securitization reporting.
  • Evaluate billing and settlement accuracy with the asset management and O&M teams, reconciling metered, monitored, and invoiced quantities and resolving discrepancies at the source.
  • Investigate underperformance to root cause across inverters, meters, communications, energy storage, and site conditions, and drive corrective work to closure with O&M and field services.
  • Direct the data requirements for fleet performance — tags, granularity, units, timestamps, and quality rules — and support data collection, ingestion, and reconciliation with the data platform team.
  • Advise on the development of Power BI dashboards and performance reporting, defining metric definitions, calculation logic, and acceptance criteria, and validating output rather than building the reports directly.
  • Define monitoring, revenue-grade metering, and telemetry requirements for new and retrofitted sites, and validate commissioning data before a site is accepted into the fleet.
  • Establish performance baselines and data mappings for newly acquired or transitioned portfolios, including migration from legacy monitoring platforms.
  • Validate storage system performance against contracted operating modes, including dispatch behavior, state of health, cycling, and demand-charge and tariff-driven response.
  • Apply AI tooling and agentic workflows to accelerate fleet diagnostics, anomaly triage, and recurring analysis, and define where model output requires engineering verification before it is relied on.
  • Serve as technical reviewer for warranty, insurance, and equipment claims requiring quantified production loss, and mentor junior engineers and analysts on performance methods.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering, physics, or a related technical field.
  • 8+ years in solar or storage performance engineering, asset performance management, or renewable O&M engineering, including 3+ years supporting commercial or utility-scale assets.
  • Hands-on experience with PV performance modeling in PlantPredict (PVsyst or SAM acceptable as a secondary), and with satellite irradiance and weather datasets including Solcast, SolarAnywhere, and Open-Meteo.
  • Working experience with fleet monitoring and asset performance platforms including AlsoEnergy, Power Factors, and 3E, including data extraction, tag mapping, and alarm configuration.
  • Proficiency in SQL and in Python for engineering analysis (pandas, numpy, pvlib or equivalent).
  • Practical fluency with AI tooling — coding assistants, LLM-based analysis, and agentic workflows — applied to engineering work, with sound judgment on where output must be verified.
  • Demonstrated ability to specify data requirements, validation rules, and reconciliation logic for engineering and BI teams, and to review dashboards and reporting for correctness.
  • Working knowledge of monitoring, metering, and SCADA data acquisition, including common protocols and vendor APIs (Modbus, SunSpec, DNP3, REST).
  • Familiarity with leased, PPA, and securitized portfolios, including production and availability guarantees, settlement mechanics, and investor reporting obligations.
  • Battery energy storage experience covering BMS behavior, state-of-health analysis, and dispatch validation.
  • Ability to work against incomplete legacy as-built and monitoring data, and to state assumptions and uncertainty explicitly to engineering, asset management, and capital partners.
